extracted.intended_audience: Congress, USPTO leadership, patent practitioners, agency stakeholders, and the public interested in patent quality and agency accountability
extracted.subtask_short: patent quality and agency compliance standards
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and criteria the USPTO uses to ensure high-quality patents, timely PTAB decisions, IT and financial system compliance, fee management, and fiscal/internal control governance. Covers procedural rules (e.g., maintenance fees, deferred revenue), statutory compliance (FMFIA/FFMIA/FISMA/DATA Act), and operational metrics (pendency, renewal rates, operating reserves).

rubrics_metrics.name: High-quality patents
rubrics_metrics.description: High-quality patents, that is, patents that are correctly issued in compliance with all requirements of Title 35 as well as the relevant case law at the time of issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures certainty and clarity of rights, fuels innovation, and reduces needless litigation. The Enhanced Patent Quality Initiative (EPQI) launched to improve accuracy, clarity, consistency of issued patents and how patent quality is measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced Patent Quality Initiative (EPQI) programs and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: A multifaceted initiative that includes almost a dozen programs aimed at improving the accuracy, clarity, and consistency of patents that are issued, as well as how patent quality is measured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO resources to facilitate collaboration and engagement: monthly patent quality chats hosted by the Office of the Deputy Commissioner of Patent Quality; detailed interview practices information including free video conferencing with USPTO examiners; updated examination guidance and training materials; and a patent ombudsman program assisting applicants/representatives during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder engagement and collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Continued engagement and collaboration with internal and external stakeholders is critical to bring meaningful change and accessibility to all aspects of the IP ecosystem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accomplished through outreach, testimony to oversight groups, and public explanations of USPTO functions; sharing fee adjustment proposals with PPAC/TPAC and the public as part of fee setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB AIA implementation and timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain PTAB’s ability to provide timely and high-quality decisions under AIA dispute resolution provisions, including meeting the AIA’s 12-month pendency requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenges include increased workload from AIA post-issuance proceedings and changes allowing patent owners to submit new testimonial evidence. USPTO reports continued meeting of statutory deadlines and references Goal I, Objective 7 for further discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on information technology to enable mission
rubrics_metrics.description: IT is a mission-critical enabler for every aspect of USPTO operations; quality, efficiency, and productivity of patent and trademark operations depend on IT system performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiyear upgrades to business systems and infrastructure to support 24/7/365 operations, improved examination and revenue-collection capabilities, recovery capabilities, successful/reliable IT deployments, and better understanding of IT interactions with performance, services, and data.

rubrics_metrics.name: IT infrastructure resilience and continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract for clean uninterrupted power from state of the art, redundant, uninterrupted power supplies for data systems to avoid outages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO analyzes outages (e.g., Dec 22, 2015 power outage) to eliminate concerns of foul play, learn lessons, and implement improvements with service providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: IT security continuous monitoring and FISMA compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: IT Security Program strategy for continuous monitoring includes quarterly credentialed compliance and vulnerability scans and ensuring operating systems are configured per security baselines and appropriate patch levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop new secure baseline configuration guides; integrate artifacts to support Security Impact Analysis within the systems development lifecycle to assess testing requirements for systems undergoing development/enhancements/maintenance. USPTO reported all systems achieved a 100 percent FISMA compliance reporting level for FY 2016; no deficiencies considered material weaknesses in internal control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives of internal control (FMFIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The objectives of internal control are to ensure: (1) Effectiveness and efficiency of operations; (2) Reliability of financial reporting; and (3) Compliance with laws and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement of assurance is based on evaluations, control assessments, reconciliations, audits (DOC OIG), and independent public accountants’ opinion; USPTO certified reasonable assurance that internal control over operations, reporting, and compliance was operating effectively as of Sept 30, 2016.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial compliance with federal financial management requirements (FFMIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantial compliance is achieved when an agency’s financial management systems routinely provide reliable and timely financial information for managing day-to-day operations as well as to produce reliable financial statements, maintain effective internal control, and comply with legal and regulatory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO complied substantially with FFMIA for FY 2016 per OMB Circular A-123, Appendix D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper payments risk assessment and remediation
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain internal control procedures to help monitor disbursement of federal funds and assess improper payment risks covering all programs and activities as required by OMB Circular A-123, Appendix C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improper payment risk assessments include assessment of control and procurement environments, are updated on a continuous/annual basis, and remediation details are provided in the Other Information section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt Payment Act compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Report on efforts to make timely payments to vendors, including interest penalties for late payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO tracked timely processing of invoices (99.8 percent timely in FY 2016), reported interest penalties on late invoices, and processed recurring payments by EFT per Debt Collection Improvement Act provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debt collection and delinquent debt handling (Debt Collection Improvement Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for administrative collection, compromise, suspension, termination, and referral for litigation of federal agency collection actions; referral to proper agency for litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although minimal delinquent debt at USPTO, all debt more than 120 days old transferred to U.S. Department of the Treasury for cross-servicing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biennial review of fees and Activity Based Costing
rubrics_metrics.description: Require a biennial review of agency fees, rents, and other charges to identify activities for charging fees and to periodically adjust fees to reflect current costs or market value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO is a fully fee-funded agency and uses Activity Based Costing (ABC) to calculate the cost of activities for each fee and uses this to inform fee setting; consistent with AIA, USPTO will assess fees at least biennially and has shared proposals with advisory committees and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: DATA Act reporting and data standards compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Report financial and payment data in accordance with data standards established by the Department of Treasury and OMB under the DATA Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO houses required budget, financial spending, and award data in a single source system; implementation activities include extracting, validating, and reconciling data prior to submission with minimal operational business process changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Management Systems modernization strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and evolve the Consolidated Financial System (CFS) and replace legacy fee collection system (RAM) with Fee Processing Next Generation (FPNG) to support financial management, fee collections, procurement, and travel functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFS leverages COTS/GOTS products and internally developed systems; FPNG (planned final release FY 2018) aims to provide automated internal controls, electronic commerce capabilities, modern UI consistent with other USPTO websites, and to meet future patent and trademark fee collection needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferred revenue calculation methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Deferred revenue liability is calculated by analyzing the process for completing each fee service provided and applying the percent incomplete based on inventory of pending work and completion status to fee collections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferred revenue includes unearned patent and trademark fees and undeposited checks; changes in filings, first action pendency, total pendency, and fee rates impact deferred revenue amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earned revenue recognition for fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee collections are recognized as earned revenue when the activities to complete the work associated with the fee are completed; maintenance fees are recognized immediately as earned revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Earned revenue composition example: maintenance fees, prior-year deferred fees, work performed during the fiscal year, and non-fee-related revenue; maintenance fees reflect patent issue levels from prior years and can significantly impact matching costs and revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fee payment rules and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance fees must be paid at three intervals (3.5, 7.5, and 11.5 years from issue). Failure to pay results in lapse of patent protection; payments are made in a six-month window preceding each due date or in a six-month grace period after due date with surcharge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fees are not paid timely and patent owner desires reinstatement, a petition and proper fees are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring patent renewal rates and factors affecting renewals
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO closely monitors payment behaviors (rates of renewal and timing) to forecast maintenance fee revenue and analyses renewal trends across first, second, and third stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewal decisions are influenced by federal court decisions, IP budgets, perceived patent value, and the economy; USPTO reports observed minor downward trends in renewal rates and uses preliminary data until full calendar year data available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating reserve management and statutory separation
rubrics_metrics.description: As required by 35 U.S.C. § 42(c)(3), USPTO maintains and tracks separate operating reserve balances for Patent operations and Trademark operations to permit planning for long-term financial stability and manage cash flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operating reserve provides resources to sustain operations early in the fiscal year when fee collections are low, is used for investments (e.g., IT improvements), and reported in months of operating expenses for transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pendency metrics and their impact on finances
rubrics_metrics.description: First action pendency and total pendency are tracked; changes in pendency affect deferred revenue and earned revenue recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decreases in first action or total pendency decrease deferred revenue (more work completed sooner) and can increase earned revenue; pendency projections are included in budget forecasts (e.g., FY 2017 President’s Budget projections).
